_comment: Greenhollow town runtime config. Cells are the 65x65 town grid; an NPC cell is the character's FEET (bottom-centre), matching scripts/render_town_hero_proof.py and scripts/place_town_npcs.py. ids and dialogueKeys are FIXED by the frozen bundle -- kikisChallenge turns in against npc id `kiki` here -- so they are never renamed to match the art.

npcs.name: Elder Rowan
npcs.text: Welcome home, child. Greenhollow is safe, but the world beyond the gate is not. Follow the south road to Millbrook when you are ready, and mind the woods.

npcs.name: Kiki
npcs.text: You want to be an adventurer? Prove it! Take my challenge, answer what I ask out on the road, and come back here to claim your reward.

npcs.name: Healer
npcs.text: Come in whenever you are hurt. I will mend you, and it costs you nothing here in Greenhollow.

npcs.name: Villager
npcs.text: Save your progress at the well before you leave. Everyone forgets once, and only once.

npcs.name: Villager
npcs.text: Monsters roam outside the palisade now. Fight them and you will grow stronger, but run if a fight turns against you.

npcs.name: Fisherman
npcs.text: The stream runs down to Millbrook, and the mill folk trade well. Long walk, though. Pack something to eat.

npcs.name: Shopkeeper
npcs.text: Take a look at my wares, traveller.

exit.note: Exit lands on the overworld, and the AUTHORITY is public/act1-world-map.js's LANDMARKS entry for this town -- `EXITS[mapId] = L.exit`, the open cell beside its door. NOT src/data/maps.ts. maps.ts's connection (60,341) is legacy: the Act 1 override REWRITES it at runtime, but only inside scene.checkTransition, which is the SHIPPED town's edge-exit path. A hi-fi town never goes through it -- adapter.js's act1-town-exit handler assigns scene.heroTileX/heroTileY = data.toX/toY directly -- so for these towns the value here is used RAW and must already be the landmark exit. || IN-TOWN HALF RE-MEASURED 2026-08-24 AGAINST THE PAINTING. Owner, on build 57: "the in-town exit does not match what we see on screen." He was right, and it was the same defect in all three towns: `cell` sat 2.5-3.5 cells BEYOND the drawn gate, out on the open trail, so the player walked visibly out of the village and kept going before the screen changed. Millbrook's fence line measures at cell y=56 by timber_mask (12.6 / 21.5 / 10.6 % of rows 55/56/57 against under 1% either side); greenhollow's at y=55.5; Port Sapphire has no gate and its mouth is where the trail leaves the frame at y=0. The old cells -- 60.5, 59.0 and 3.0 -- predate the current paintings. || `cell` is now the GATE AS PAINTED and `startCell` is 3.5 cells INSIDE it. That combination is what makes town.html's arming work without a code change: it arms once the player is more than 2.5 cells clear, so a 3.5-cell spawn is armed on arrival but outside the dy<1.0 / dx<1.6 fire box, and the exit then fires exactly when she steps into the gate. The previous arrangement solved the same arming problem the other way round -- exit outside, spawn on the gate -- which is what put the trigger out in the grass. || The OVERWORLD half (toX/toY) is unchanged and still gated by scripts/check_town_transitions.py.

_dialogueNote: name/text are English FALLBACK strings in the voice of the shipped Port Sapphire entries, so the town is playable standalone. The runtime also posts act1-town-interact to the parent, so the frozen bundle's localised dialogue system takes over once the adapter hands off -- which is why dialogueKey must stay exactly as the bundle has it.
_startNote: MOVED 2026-08-24 from [32.5, 57.0] to [32.5, 52.0]: 3.5 cells inside the painted gate, which is what arms the exit on arrival without firing it. See exit.note.
_serviceNote: shopCounter stands on the lane below the striped awning, and shopId matches the inventory src/data/shops.ts already defines. Both were None, so the shop was unreachable even though the map data expected it.
_layoutNote: REPLACED 2026-08-22. These cells no longer come from design/act1-towns/greenhollow/spec.json: scripts/town_layout.py wrote it for the plan-primed layout the owner scrapped, and the village was repainted afterwards, so its snapping described geometry the art no longer has. Towns are ART-FIRST -- the painting is authored, scripts/derive_town_walkable.py derives collision from the finished plate, and scripts/place_town_actors.py places actors against THAT, eroding by actorFootRadius so the body fits and flood-filling from startCell so nothing stands somewhere the player cannot reach. villager1 and villager2 were CHOSEN by hand rather than auto-snapped: their old cells landed on the market stall's counter and the herbalist's porch in the painted village, and the nearest standable ground was 5.1 and 5.7 cells away, far enough that the snap would have decided the composition instead of reporting it.
_shopkeeperNote: MOVED OUT IN FRONT 2026-08-24. Owner, on build 58: "the shop keeper is placed on top of the shop so lets put him in front of the shop." He was standing INSIDE the stall, three to four cells above shopCounter and level with the hanging produce, which from a top-down camera reads as standing ON the stall rather than behind its counter -- the 2026-08-22 note below asked for him to be findable in his shop and this was the wrong way to give him that. He now stands on the lane beside the counter, on ground the player walks on, so he is a person in front of a shop. || `fixed` is DROPPED with him: it existed only because the inside of a stall is deliberately not walkable and snapping him would have thrown him out onto the lane -- which is now where he is meant to be. scripts/place_town_actors.py places and validates him like every other NPC, including the talk-band check. || Tapping him still opens the shipped ShopScene rather than a dialogue box, so the town never forks the inventory or the prices, and shopCounter remains the service spot in front of the stall. || PREVIOUS NOTE: Owner 2026-08-22: "i cannot find the shopkeeper and the shopkeeper needs to be in a shop." He stands INSIDE the market stall, behind the counter, which is why he carries `fixed: true` -- scripts/place_town_actors.py snaps actors onto walkable ground and the inside of a stall is deliberately not walkable, so snapping him would put him out on the lane. town.html routes a tap on him to the shop the same way it routes the healer to the heal flow, so the shipped ShopScene stays the single implementation. shopCounter remains the spot in FRONT of the stall where the player stands.
_firstEntryNote: OWNER 2026-08-25 (build 59): 'the initial starting position of the hero does not make sense. The hero needs to start the game in front of the elder, facing him, at interacting distance.' This is the NEW-GAME opening only -- it is deliberately NOT `startCell`, which is the ARRIVAL cell used every time the player walks in from the overworld and is positioned 3.5 cells inside the painted gate so the exit arms without firing (see _startNote). Using one field for both would teleport the player to the elder on every re-entry. Elder Rowan stands at [32.19,21.81]; this is 1.8 cells due south of him (1.2 was measured on screen and the two sprites overlapped), which is inside nearestNpc()'s south approach band (|dx| <= 1.1 cells, 0 < dy <= 2.1) and clear of his 7 world-px block radius, so the greeting prompt is up on the first frame. Facing 'up' so she is looking at him, not away.
